title: Missing middle housing study and two high-rise rezonings
subtitle: Also covered: townhouses at 1385 Bleams Road, King Street East and Mill Street towers, Bill 23 deadlines.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended that a feasibility study on missing middle and affordable housing guide the Growing Together planning work for major transit station areas, future Official Plan and zoning updates, and process improvements. Staff are also to consider financial incentives and report back once Bill 23 rules on affordable and attainable housing are clearer {{vote:m2}}.

The committee also recommended approving two large mixed-use projects near light rail stations. One is at 1001 King Street East, near the Borden station {{vote:m3}}. The other is at 455-509 Mill Street, beside the Mill station, which includes a commitment to 50 affordable rental units and a community space {{vote:m4}}. Both change land use and zoning and adopt urban design briefs. The Official Plan amendments go to the Region of Waterloo for approval.

The committee recommended zoning approval for eight townhouses beside a heritage home at 1385 Bleams Road {{vote:m1}}. It was the City's first application subject to the Bill 23 90-day decision deadline, with a fee refund if missed.
All of these are recommendations. They go to Council for a final decision, and staff said the Bleams Road item would go to a Special Council meeting the same evening.

decisions.item: Missing middle and affordable housing study
decisions.detail: The committee recommended using the feasibility study to inform Growing Together, Official Plan and zoning updates and development process improvements, and directed staff to consider financial incentives and report back after more Bill 23 information is available.

The committee recommended adopting an Official Plan amendment, approving a zoning amendment and adopting an urban design brief for a mixed-use development, with the Official Plan amendment forwarded to the Region of Waterloo.

The committee recommended changing the designation from general industrial employment to mixed use, approving the zoning amendment and adopting the urban design brief, to be applied through site plan approval.
The committee recommended approving a zoning by-law amendment to allow eight townhouses on part of a property that keeps its existing heritage home.

debate: On the housing study, a number of councillors urged staff to be bold and to look beyond the transit station areas, including citywide. Staff said the first phase focuses on those areas because of existing transit investment and work already planned, with Official Plan changes to follow.

Some councillors questioned parking reductions, saying transit may not keep up with growth, especially in the suburbs. Staff and consultants replied that not every household owns a car, and that a mix of options and timing of infrastructure matter.

One councillor was concerned that financial incentives could mean taxpayer money helping investors build. Staff said no direction is set, the provincial rules limit what incentives are allowed, and options would return to Council.

On the King Street East and Mill Street towers, one councillor raised neighbourhood compatibility, traffic and the pace of change in nearby areas. The Mill Street developer pointed to stepped heights, a transit-focused design and a traffic study that raised no concerns.

At Bleams Road, councillors asked about archaeology and removed visitor parking. The applicant said artifacts found were mainly tied to the former schoolhouse, and that driveways, an internal road and nearby short-term parking would serve visitors.
